run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Make `Field.Control` sync dirty/filled/validation with controlled `value` changes (mount reads aside, typed updates, and programmatic updates) via `useValueChanged`, matching how Switch, Checkbox, Checkbox Group, Radio Group, Select, Slider, Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field already integrate with field state; and fix two riders: a dirty flag that never cleared for non-string controlled values, and `details.cancel()` being ignored in the uncontrolled `onChange` path.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; the supplied PR body is the only intent source. Every explicit outcome it names is implemented and covered by a passing added test, except the 'same shape as its siblings' / 'a controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field' claim: the value FieldControl now hands `useRegisterFieldControl` is the DOM-serialized string instead of the raw typed value every one of those siblings passes, which is the confirmed finding below.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (2/2 changed files, 2/2 diff chunks, no truncation). FieldControl.test.tsx's full 27-case suite run at the pinned head in the reviewed clone: 26 passed, 1 skipped (isJSDOM-gated SSR autofocus case). One candidate verified by a fresh-context worker plus a focused scratch-vitest reproduction I ran at head and again against the merge-base FieldControl.tsx to confirm the regression is introduced by this diff.

findings.title: Controlled non-string values reach validate() as strings on submit
findings.trigger: Mount `<Field.Root validate={fn}><Field.Control value={5} onValueChange={setValue} /></Field.Root>` inside `<Form>`, then submit the form (or call `actionsRef.validate()`) without first typing into the control.
findings.impact: `validate(value, formValues)` receives the string "5" instead of the number 5 (or a stringified array/object for other controlled types) on the submit / `actionsRef.validate()` path, breaking validate logic that relies on the original type (`value === 5`, `Array.isArray(value)`, `Number.isInteger(value)`). Confirmed with a focused jsdom test that fails at head (received value is the string "5") and passes unmodified against the merge-base FieldControl.tsx (received value is the number 5), so this is introduced by this diff, not pre-existing. Every sibling that registers a controlled value with the field (NumberFieldInput, SliderRoot, OTPFieldRoot, AriaCombobox, SelectRoot) passes the raw typed value into `useRegisterFieldControl` and uses a separate override argument only for the DOM/form-value string projection; `Field.Control` is now the only one that collapses both into the serialized string, directly contradicting this PR's own 'same shape as its siblings' claim.
findings.change: In `packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.tsx`, pass the raw controlled `value` (not `serializedValue`) as the third argument to `useRegisterFieldControl`, so `registration.value` (read by `getRegistrationValue`/`commit` for `validate`) keeps its original type; keep `serializedValue` only for the `useValueChanged` dirty/filled comparisons a few lines below. `getValueFromInput` is already the separate `getFormValueOverride` argument, so `onFormSubmit`'s DOM-string projection is unaffected by this change.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"Dirty state never cleared for non-string values."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:86 serializes the controlled value before comparison and :111 compares it to `validityData.initialValue`; the added test 'clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value' passed in the full FieldControl.test.tsx run at head.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"Programmatic changes left the field stale."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:105-115 wires `useValueChanged(serializedValue, ...)` to update dirty/filled/validation on any prop-driven value change; the added test 'syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically' passed.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"`details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling. It was ignored."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx:153 adds `!details.isCanceled` to the uncontrolled `onChange` guard; the added test 'does not validate when the change is canceled' passed. Only the uncontrolled path is exercised by a test; the controlled path achieves the same net effect architecturally (a rejected value is simply never written back to the `value` prop, so `useValueChanged` never fires), which is consistent but not separately tested.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field."
requirements.evidence: The early return at FieldControl.tsx:144-146 does keep a rejected/rewritten controlled value out of dirty/filled state, met on its own terms. The claimed parity with Number Field/Combobox/OTP Field does not hold one layer down: those siblings register the raw typed value with the field for `validate`/`commit`, while Field.Control now registers a stringified copy — see the confirmed finding `field-control/registration-value-stringified`.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"Field.Control now has the same shape as its siblings, with the residual difference being the mount-time DOM read that its uncontrolled mode requires."
requirements.evidence: Contradicted by the confirmed finding: siblings keep the registration value raw and add a separate string-projection override, which Field.Control does not.

requirements.source: spec-pr-5460-body/"Renders per keystroke for a controlled input... This PR: 2 on the first, then 1 (onSubmit); 2 per keystroke (onChange)"
requirements.evidence: The added test 'renders once per keystroke for controlled input changes' asserts the steady-state +2-renders-for-2-keystrokes invariant this table implies for the default (onSubmit) validation mode, and it passed. The full cross-mode table (including the `onChange`-mode and Number Field comparison columns) was not independently re-measured; nothing in the diff contradicts it and no reviewed candidate depends on the exact counts, so this is not raised as a question.
